_purpose: Close the DENOMINATOR GAP in research/PROSE-REFS-OR-FIELDS.md. That analysis measured rows-vs-prose over ID CANDIDATES IN THE CORPUS (93.6% / 6.4%). The VALUE claim for story 12 is 21.8% of THE ADVERSARY'S FINDINGS, which is a different denominator and does not transfer. This file re-classifies every class-C finding in fstar_hand_sample.json by WHICH INSTRUMENT WOULD CATCH IT.
_method: Hand-read, one at a time, asking a single question per finding: what would a checker need in order to REPORT this? Not keyword rules — FSTAR-COMPARISON records that keyword rules classified only 33% of findings and that a 33% rate cannot support a verdict.

_verdicts.12a: caught by making the REFERENT a row/field with typed links; the disagreement becomes a join, or becomes impossible
_verdicts.12b: needs BODY-PROSE extraction: a literal inlined in narrative, a section reference, a format/wording divergence
_verdicts.neither: requires SEMANTIC JUDGEMENT even with rows; rows make the pairing mechanical but not the verdict

_caveat: n=19. A 7/19 share carries roughly +/-22 points at 95%, so the ORDERING between 12a and 12b is NOT established by this — only that they are comparable and that neither is a small residual.

findings.why: an AC identifier cited by a BC has gone stale. With AC rows keyed (story, ac_id) and a typed link, a stale citation is a dangling foreign key.
